history.period: Ancient consecration legend; Pandya-era masonry structure (date unverified)
history.summary: UNUSUAL DEDICATION FLAG: this temple is dedicated to Rajarishi Vishwamitra (a sage), not a conventional deity - an uncommon dedication in Tamil Nadu. CSV TOWN FLAG: the CSV gives town as Tirunelveli, but the temple is at Vijayapathi (Vijayapati), Radhapuram taluk, Tirunelveli district, on the Bay of Bengal seashore about 70 km south of Tirunelveli city. It is famed as a parikara sthalam for papa doshas (the '64 types of papa dosham' sthalam). Legend: after consecrating Kali Devi in the Thillai forest to remove the Brahmahathi dosha of Rama and Lakshmana, Vishwamitra came south, placed the goddess Kali Devi in a grove at Vijayapati, and consecrated Hom Kunda Vinayakar, Vishwamitra Mahalinga Swami and Akilandeswari Ambal in the sacred homakundam; a Pandya king who learned of this built the temple and set his fish emblem inside. Vishwamitra Maharishi is believed to meditate here. The east-facing gopuram carries idols of Shiva, Parvati, Ganesha, Murugan, Vishvamithrar and Nandhi. On new-moon and Amavasya days thousands bathe at the Vishwamithra Theertha in the sea and perform pongal poojas at the Thillaikkali temple.

name: Vishwamitra Temple
town_description: Vijayapathi is a coastal village in Radhapuram taluk of Tirunelveli district, about 70 km south of Tirunelveli city on the Bay of Bengal, near Idinthakarai and Koodankulam, known for its seashore temples and fishing community.

travel.airport: Trivandrum International Airport (~95 km) or Tuticorin Airport (~85 km) are the nearest options.
travel.railway: Valliyur (Vadakkuvalliyur) railway station, about 27 km away, is the nearest.
travel.road: 5QR3+QQ7, Vijayapathi, Tirunelveli 627104; on the seashore near Idinthakarai, reachable by road from Tirunelveli via Radhapuram; car parking for about 100 vehicles.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Amavasya and new-moon days are the most auspicious but also the most crowded.
